messages:
ryan: Heads-up — AcmeHealth reports that their quantized endpoint (model=rw-3b-q4) is serving slower and generating lower-quality responses compared to their previous fp16 endpoint. They say p95 jumped ~30% and throughput dropped ~25% after the last calibration.

jessica: Customer provided logs and request samples. Small to medium prompts (avg 150 tokens) with KV-cache enabled. They ran a simple A/B: q4 vs fp16. FP16 p95 ~120ms, Q4 p95 ~160ms.

samir: @jessica can you paste the exact model id + config they used and whether we pushed any kernel/driver changes in their region last 48h?

jessica: Model: rw-3b-q4-calib-2026-03-10. Serving config: batching.window_ms=25, batching.max_batch=8, kv_cache=true, kernel_policy=auto. No infra driver updates in the region. We did roll out a quant kernel tweak two days ago (runtime:kernel-select v2.7) but can confirm which clusters got it.

lee: Profiling snapshot I pulled from a repro request on internal canary:
```
Request id: 0d9f
Sequence len: 150
Kernel chosen: quant_forward_q4_kernel (layer groups 3-12)
Layer latency breakdown (ms): 4bit-kernel: 78, matmul: 22, kv-update: 18, overhead/dispatch: 42
Total p95: 162ms
```
The 4bit kernel we defaulted to appears to be memory-bound for these sequence lengths; fp16 uses a different tiled matmul that is faster here.

maria: Also saw increased KV cache churn for this customer. Their request traffic pattern has many short-lived contexts (lots of unique conversation ids), so token reuse is low -> quant kernels don't amortize well. Shipping quant with small batches + low KV reuse may lose the win.

samir: Important note: kernel-policy=auto currently prefers q4 kernels when quantized weights are present. If sequence_len < 256 and batch < 4 we should prefer fp16-tiled kernel. That heuristic didn't kick because the calibration metadata flagged 'low-quality fallback' disabled.

ryan: Customer asked for immediate mitigation. Suggested: 1) temp pin them to fp16 model, 2) adjust server-side kernel routing, or 3) raise batching.window_ms to increase batching. Which is quickest?

lee: Fastest is kernel routing change (server side) — flip policy for their tenant to prefer fp16 for small batches. Rolling that out takes ~10-15m and no model redeploy. Pinning to fp16 endpoint is a bit slower (requires tenant routing change and validation). Bumping window_ms will increase latency for other users but could help throughput.

samir: I'll prepare a canary config:
```json
{ "kernel_policy_override": "prefer_fp16_small_batches", "batching": { "window_ms": 50, "max_batch": 8 } }
```
We'll apply to a single customer shard, run repro requests, compare p95.

jessica: I'll message AcmeHealth that we're investigating and propose two immediate options: quick routing flip to fp16 canary (ETA 30m) or a rollback to their previous fp16 stable endpoint. They opted for the routing flip first.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0479 — "AcmeHealth quantized endpoint throughput regression" (owner: samir).

lee: After canary flip results: q4 p95=160ms, fp16-canary p95=118ms, throughput +28% on canary. Kernel selection trace shows fp16 tiled kernels used for most matmuls.

maria: We'll also add a short-term metric: per-tenant kv_reuse_ratio and batch_size distribution to detect customers likely to regress on Q4. Recommend a routing rule: if kv_reuse_ratio < 0.3 AND median_batch_size < 4 -> prefer fp16.

samir: Agreed. Longer-term: need a small release to update kernel_policy heuristics and include calibration metadata that suggests when quantization is expected to win (based on sequence length, kv reuse, batch shape). I'll open a PR and link tests.

jessica: Customer updated: they see improved latency on canary, appreciate fast response. We'll follow up with formal RCA and plan for a calibration sweep to try alternative scale/clamp params before re-enabling q4.

ryan: Thanks everyone. Action items: samir -> PR for policy heuristics, lee -> rollout plan for tenant routing change (done in canary), maria -> add KV/batch metrics to tenant dashboard, jessica -> customer comms + follow-up.

samir: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/2319 (wip). Tests include microbench for seq_len 32/128/512 and keys:kv_reuse scenarios.

lee: Note for the record — calibration can sometimes produce weight stats that lead the selector to pick a different kernel group which is suboptimal at certain seq/batch shapes. We should treat kernel selection and calibration as a joint optimization, not independent steps. :thinking_face:

jessica: Marking thread resolved for customer for now; will reopen if perf changes after calibration sweep. :white_check_mark:
